title: Accounts Standard: Tenants Holding Several Vehicle, RV & Boat Parking Agreements
content:
A tenant may hold more than one Vehicle, RV & Boat Parking Agreement. For such a tenant the company applies the following standard.

1. **Review agreement by agreement.** Each agreement is reviewed on its own: it keeps its own start date, its own rent change history and its own increase eligibility. An increase on one agreement never makes another agreement eligible for an increase.
2. **Retention concessions counted per agreement.** Where the tenant asks for a retention concession on several agreements, each agreement's concession is counted against that agreement's own allowance, not against a shared allowance.
3. **Applying a payment that names no space.** A payment that does not name a space is applied first to the agreement with the earliest delinquency date (the due date of its oldest unpaid period), then to the remaining agreements in order of start date, oldest first. The allocation basis is therefore: earliest delinquency date first, then oldest start date.

### Illustration (hypothetical agreements)

A tenant holds three agreements and makes a payment without naming a space:

| Agreement | Delinquency date | Start date | Order of application |
|---|---|---|---|
| Space A | 1 March | 10 January two years ago | First (earliest delinquency date) |
| Space B | none (not delinquent) | 5 May three years ago | Second (oldest start date among the rest) |
| Space C | none (not delinquent) | 20 August last year | Third |

Had Space B also carried a delinquency date, the two delinquency dates would be compared first; the start dates order only the agreements that remain.

### Basis Q&A

- *Does an increase noticed on one of the tenant's spaces open the interval for another space?* No; each agreement's increase eligibility rests on its own start date and rent change history.
- *If a tenant has already received a concession on one space this year, is that counted on a second space?* No; each concession is counted against the allowance of the agreement it was given on.
